summary:
Your volume has been remarkably stable — 127 km over the last four weeks against 125 km the prior block, effectively flat — but the internal structure of those weeks is telling a clearer story. The 44 km effort on June 8th anchors the recent period, and the June 27th session at 4:49/km with HR 161 represents a distinctly different quality tier from the aerobic recovery work on either side of it. These aren't undifferentiated kilometres; the distribution shows you're maintaining both ends of the stimulus spectrum within a consistent volume envelope.

Today's 13.77 km at 5:48/km and HR 137 sits comfortably at the low-aerobic end — compare it to June 30th's similar effort (11.73 km, 5:59/km, HR 143) and the pattern is consistent easy running with controlled cardiac response. What's worth noting is that a freshly updated lactate threshold of 4:24/km at 178 bpm gives you a concrete internal anchor now — your easy runs are sitting roughly 84 seconds/km below threshold pace, which is appropriate spacing for genuine recovery and aerobic base work.

The 20-week running streak matching your personal best and a strength session count of 34 year-to-date (well ahead of last year's baseline context) both point to the kind of structural consistency that compounds quietly. Four strength sessions in the last four weeks is modest relative to the available training days — worth monitoring whether that's deliberate management or just scheduling drift.
